references.text: The preceding context describing the engraving of the names of Israel's sons on the two onyx stones that were to be attached to the shoulders of the ephod.
Aaron shall carry the names of Israel's sons on the breastplate over his heart as a constant reminder before the Lord, parallel to carrying the names on the shoulders.
The fulfillment of the command to set the onyx stones on the shoulders of the ephod as memorial stones for Israel's sons.
The concept of being a reminder before God's face, where Israel is remembered by God.
The stones from Jordan as memorial stones (זִכָּרוֹן) for the children of Israel, the same theme of memorial stones.
The Lord has engraved Israel on His palms, an image that God continually remembers His people, parallel to Aaron carrying the names.
The description of the ephod itself to which the shoulder stones were to be attached.
Jesus as our high priest intercedes for us and presents us before God, a perfect fulfillment of Aaron's priestly service.
The historical fulfillment of the command to attach the stones as memorial stones.
Contrast between carrying the people for remembrance (shoulders) and bearing iniquity concerning holy gifts (forehead).
Complementary role: to carry the people for remembrance (shoulders) and to bear judgment over his heart.
Explains the content of the memorial stones: the names of the twelve tribes representing the entire nation.
